notes: Fiscus — a local-first personal money ledger built with vanilla HTML/CSS/JS: no frameworks, no build step, zero runtime dependencies. Five hash-routed views (Dashboard, Transactions, Budgets, Reports, Settings) share one validated data store: transaction CRUD with inline form validation and undo for deletions, per-category monthly budgets with copy-forward, SVG trend/donut charts with screen-reader summaries, derived insights, and duplicate-name guards. Data portability via JSON backup export/import (merge or replace, fully validated with a preview step and per-record skip report) and CSV export. Persistence uses localStorage with probe detection, an in-memory session fallback with a visible banner, safe reset on corrupted data, and a storage-status panel. Accessibility: keyboard-navigable modals with focus trapping and restore, Escape handling, skip link, aria-live regions, focus management after actions, and a responsive layout with a bottom nav bar and 40px+ touch targets on coarse pointers. Strictly local-only by design and disclosed in-app: there is no backend, no sync, and no network calls; the currency selector changes formatting only (no conversion); deleting a category moves its transactions to Uncategorised. Verified by driving the app in a desktop Chromium browser over a local HTTP server (navigation, CRUD, budgets, reports, settings, reload persistence, empty states); the code uses classic scripts and no fetch, so opening index.html directly from disk should also work, but that mode was not verified here. Not audited in Safari/Firefox or on real touch hardware.
